findings.passage: We face difficult challenges – specifically when it comes to protecting our communities and environment, enabling people to live healthy lives, ensuring elections are fair and free, and ensuring no one is left behind.
findings.note: Campaign home page lists fair and free elections among her challenges. It does not mention photo ID, mail-ballot ID or proof of citizenship. Date is the date the page was fetched; the page is undated.

findings.motion: Second Reading, SB 747 Elections Law Changes
findings.note: Senate roll call #300 lists her among the no votes (28 yes, 19 no). The bill text (S747v6, SL 2023-140) requires photo ID plus a proof-of-residence document for same-day registration at early voting, sets ID photocopy or affidavit rules for absentee ballots, lets an absentee ballot request use a driver license number, state ID number or last four digits of a Social Security number, and requires the State Board to review citizenship status of people excused from jury duty as non-citizens.
subjects: ID with mail or absentee ballot

findings.motion: Motion 9 To Concur in House committee substitute and House amendments, SB 747 Elections Law Changes
findings.note: Senate roll call #439 lists her among the no votes (27 yes, 18 no) on final passage of the House version, which the Governor then vetoed on 8/24/2023.
subjects: ID with mail or absentee ballot

findings.motion: Motion 11 Veto Override, SB 747 Elections Law Changes
findings.note: Senate roll call #482 lists her among the no votes on overriding the veto (30 yes, 19 no). The bill became SL 2023-140.
subjects: ID with mail or absentee ballot

findings.motion: Second Reading, HB 958 Election Law Changes
findings.note: Senate roll call #693 lists her among the no votes (28 yes, 13 no). The ratified text (H958v9) bars a county board from processing a voter registration unless the applicant affirms U.S. citizenship, sets a 30-day mailed-form fix with a statement under penalty of perjury for blank answers, and directs removal of voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database check. The Governor vetoed it on 8/17/2026.

subjects: ID or ID number with mail or absentee ballot
citizenship statement or proof to register
